data.name: Amritpal
data.gender_notes: Amritpal is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Amrit (Nectar) + Pal (Protector): The one who protects and bestows the nectar of the universe. The name Amritpal carries the meaning “Nectar of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Punjabi. Parents who choose Amritpal usually hope their child will grow to embody nectar of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine nectar of immortality and prosperity, and the protector who grants it.
data.etymology: Amritpal belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Nectar of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amritpal total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Krishna is a popular deity in the Hindu religion and is considered the eighth avatar of the god Vishnu. He is known for his mischievous acts in the Mahabharata and is a symbol of love, divinity, and eternal youth.
data.spiritual_significance: Krishna represents the Divine Play or Lila, the infinite joy and the highest truth of spiritual realization. He transcends the duality of good and evil, and embodies the concept of "unconditional love".
data.spiritual_symbolism: Amritpal: One who is filled with the divine nectar of immortality. The name signifies a deep connection with the divine, and a longing for eternal spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Amritpal was a prominent Sikh warrior and a devotee of Guru Arjun Dev. He played a crucial role in the Battle of Amritsar (1574) and was later appointed as the leader of the Sikh army during the reign of Guru Hargobind (1595-1644).

Amritpal is also mentioned in the Sikh historical text 'Bansavali' as a descendant of the legendary Sikh warrior Bhai Mardana. He is described as a brave and skilled warrior who fought against the Mughal empire during the reign of Emperor Aurangzeb (1658-1707).

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Amritpal continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
